sentences.text: Echinochimaera curva was a small holocephalan fish that grew to under 30 cm in length.
If the isolated fin spine truly belongs to an echinochimaerid, it would be the earliest known member of that group.
The type locality for the species is the St. Louis Formation of Indiana, United States.
A fin spine recovered from the Viséan beds of the same formation was tentatively assigned to a new species, Echinochimaera curva sp. nov.
Its rounded body, large pectoral fins, a pair of dorsal fins—one bearing a movable spine—and a paddle-shaped tail suggest a slow-swimming mode of life and a likely non-predatory habit.
The morphology of the fin spine closely matches that of Echinochimaera meltoni, indicating a possible close relationship within the family.
Echinochimaera is assigned to the family Echinochimaeridae within the cartilaginous fish class Chondrichthyes.
The species lived during the Viséan stage of the Carboniferous period.
The genus as a whole is known from the Lower Carboniferous, about 355 million years ago.
Its broader temporal range extends from 326.9 to 323.6 million years ago in the Serpukhovian stage.
